title: ExplainerEngineProductionScriptV4
description: Canonical Single Source of Truth (SSOT) contract for Explainer Engine v4.0 (D-123, 12-minute Z1-Z5 / S01-S16 format) with backward-compatible validation for legacy production_script/1..4.

parallax.description: D-70 stage F: tactile chiaroscuro parallax, the near-far shift at the shot's ends as a share of the frame width (production/parallax.py; needs <picture>.depth.png, else flat)

file.description: an existing picture (relative to the script's picture folders)

engine.description: canva: filler pictures only (D-53, PV-43); made by hand in Canva, placed as a file

subject.description: who does what, with which feeling: written with the line it illustrates

refs.description: picture ids the reference painter starts from

costume.description: clothing words when the default (the visitors' era) is wrong for this picture

stand_in.description: draft only: an existing picture shown until this one is painted

tier.description: Gemini batch tier (D-52, imagegen/routing.py); default standard

tier_reason.description: premium only: why this picture needs the dearer model (PV-40)

framing.description: D-69: the camera on the staged scene; left out = read from the subject and the shot type (production/staging.py)

visible.description: D-69 (CS-10): cast ids whose faces this shot must show; left out = heroes minus partial

partial.description: D-69: cast ids seen only in part (a shoulder, a back); over_shoulder defaults to every hero after the first

change.description: D-69: what this shot changes against the shot before (an action, a gesture); the room and the seats never change

cut_away.description: D-69: a picture outside the staged room (another place, a screen, a memory): painted alone, no master frame

beat.description: a visual beat (VB rules, docs/STORY_ENGINE.md): something new on screen, on a phrase of this line, written with the line

at.description: the words of THIS line the beat lands on

offset.description: seconds after the phrase's first word starts (never a clock time: the read decides)

why.description: what in the line at that instant this beat shows (VB-03)

pos.description: where on the frame (0..1); a label or highlight points at this spot of the picture

thing.description: prop: the object named in the line

asset.description: prop: a cut-out PNG (relative to the picture folders or the repo); without one the prop is drawn as a word sticker

claim.description: claim id behind a number on screen (invariant 5)

effect.description: accent: a camera accent of production/accents.py

who.description: expression: the cast id whose face changes (default: the line's speaker)

cue.description: VB-08: the short light sound that marks this beat (audio/cues.py), or 'none' with a reason

event.description: VB-08 (/3): the story event this cue marks; on /3 a cue without an event FAILs - silence is the default

why.description: why this sound (or why none: an effect already sounds here, a quiet expression)

dramatic_change.title: Dramatic change inside a held still (BP-170)

target_duration_seconds.description: Story-driven shot duration in seconds (Accordion Pacing: 1.5s-2.5s rapid cuts in high tension, 3.0s-4.5s narrative flow, 5.5s-8.5s emotional holds). Must derive organically from the spoken audio_line duration and dramatic beat; NEVER assign a constant metronome duration across shots.

multiangle_token.description: Optional camera_angle camera token emitted by ComfyUI-geminimultiangle.

end_frame_reason.description: Required when needs_end_frame is true; must explain why start/end state transition is needed.

primary_action_count.description: Hard guardrail: exactly 1 primary physical action per simple shot.

camera_move_count.description: Hard guardrail: at most 1 camera move per shot.

selective_control.description: Populated ONLY when generation_mode == 'WAN_CONTROL'. Enforces single control modality.

video_engine_tier.description: Legacy routing label of the v4.2 archive (D-129/D-130, pending the creator's word); the v4.3 route is `route` (D-131). The Gemini video engines nobody approved are not allowed.

teaser_of.description: KP-41: ID of a later payoff shot whose rendered clip this cold-open teaser reuses without new AI generation.

teaser_trim.description: KP-41: optional [start_sec, end_sec] dramatic peak trim inside the teaser_of payoff shot.

shot_role.description: Cinematic scene coverage role (establishing, OTS, close-up turn, listener reaction, insert, action cutaway, scene exit, teaser).

route.description: v4.3 route (D-131, D-132, plan P1.4): map_action = Python map with an action layer, still_25d = picture moved by the layered 2.5D renderer with motion imitation, video = a body performs an action or a hero speaks (Q4, Q7), made by LTX-2.5 distilled on Modal (D-132). wan is D-131's name of the video route; the router rewrites it to video. Filled by explainer_engine.episode.router.

route_reason.description: why the router (or the writer, with route_locked) chose the route

route_locked.description: true = the route was chosen by hand; the router keeps it and only checks it

helper_form.description: map_action shots (MA-09): the helper form the director picked from what the words say at that moment

helper_reason.description: map_action shots (MA-09): why this form serves these words; no quota, a map repeats when the words are about places

motion_imitation.description: still_25d only (plan P5, RT-05): what moves in the layered 2.5D shot. Up to two ordered camera segments (from_frame/to_frame, W2; one path when no frames are given) (push, pull, truck, crane, orbit_small) plus handheld and rack_focus; light, atmosphere, surface and subject effects; a shake only on an impact. BP-185 asks for two moving families beyond the camera.

region.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] share of the picture; required by water_shimmer, heat_haze, foliage_sway; cloth_flap and cloud_drift need one too

origin.description: sun_shaft_drift: where the light comes from (default: the brightest part of the sky)

from_frame.description: W2: a camera segment's first frame

to_frame.description: W2: a camera segment's end frame (exclusive)

hold_frames.description: W2: frames the camera rests after the segment

at_frac.description: FA-06: the effect's moment as a share of the shot (0..1); follows a retimed shot

from_frac.description: FA-06: a camera segment's start as a share of the shot (0..1)

to_frac.description: FA-06: a camera segment's end as a share of the shot (0..1)

actions.description: map_action only (plan P4): the timed action layer over the letter-free plate, each item tied to a spoken word

from.description: a place id of episode.json places (where the action starts or happens)

to.description: a place id of episode.json places (where it goes)

unit.description: the counter's unit, said in words (people, km, years)

label.description: the text a label or a split card shows (drawn by Python, never by a picture model)

event_id.description: AV-02: the event's id, unique in the episode

until_word.description: AV-05: the action lasts until the word after this phrase starts

at_frame.description: start frame (shot-relative) when no word carries the action

via.description: route waypoints between from and to: place ids of episode.json places (W3: a validated spline)

route.description: marker_travel / supply_state / snap: the event_id of the route or supply line it rides on

claim.description: the claim id of claim_map.md that backs a shown number (counter, bar_grow, progress_bar, milestone)

values.description: bar_grow: the bars' values (each backed by the claim)

camera.description: W3: the camera's answer to this event (default: hold; zoom keeps its own move)

cues.description: AV-06: the derived start/arrival/confirmation cues of a route or a number (default auto)

domain.description: MA-01: a maritime or air route may cross water (maps/paths.validate); default land

allow_water.description: MA-01: the route may cross water without a REVIEW (a ford, a frozen lake)

sound_events.description: the shot's authored sounds that the picture does not draw (D-135 guide v2 section 3b): ambience, foley and spot effects, library first; anchored on a word (at_word, follows the read) or at_s

what.description: the event: a class id of episode/sound_plan.EVENT_CLASSES, or words that name one (AV-07)

picture_event.description: the picture reacts on this sound at at_s (plan P5.6): boom/eruption = shake + lightning, impact = shake, thunder/flash = lightning

distance.description: SP-03: the event's distance (else the composition plane or the shot size)

dur_s.description: AV-04: the sound lasts this long (a span; the take repeats under it)

event_id.description: AV-02: the event's id, unique in the episode (default <shot>.S<k>)

purpose.description: BP-55: why the sound is there (a picture_event is sync)

class.description: the class id of episode/sound_plan.EVENT_CLASSES (sound_plan.shot_events reads it before what; FA-05)

at_word.description: FA-06 / P1: the sound lands on a spoken word and follows the read when the shot is retimed: a phrase of the shot's line (as actions[].at_word) or {line_id, word (index in that line from 0, or its text), offset_s}; exactly one of at_s / at_word

map_view.description: map_action: the camera's first view (centre and width in km); without it the view fits the action places

fallback_motion_imitation.description: wan only (plan P6.2): the layered 2.5D motion the shot falls back to when its Wan clip fails QA twice; without it the fallback is a push and a subject sway, whose BP-185 row then FAILs for the creator to see

region.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] share of the picture; required by water_shimmer, heat_haze, foliage_sway

origin.description: sun_shaft_drift: where the light comes from (default: the brightest part of the sky)

motion_profile.description: W2: the shot's motion profile (how far and how fast its planes may travel)

edit_plan.description: The shot's editorial plan, written before any paid clip (VL rules, docs/VIDEO_LANE.md, D-137). Required on every route=video shot by explainer_engine.videolane.plan; optional elsewhere. How this shot joins the one before, what the camera does at its ends, where its one line sits in the clip and how much clean picture it keeps for the cut.

continuity_mode.description: continuation = the same action goes on (the next clip starts from a chosen frame of the clip before); coverage = a new camera angle on the same scene, drawn fresh from the scene master and the hero sheets; insert = a reaction, hand, object or detail (prefer still_25d)

continuity_from.description: continuation: the shot whose clip this one continues

scene_master.description: coverage/insert: the picture key of the scene's master frame (production/pictures.json)

axis_side.description: the camera's side of the scene's 180-degree axis

screen_positions.description: character_id -> where the character stands on screen

camera_in.description: what the camera does on the shot's first frames

camera_out.description: what the camera does on the shot's last frames

speech_onset_s.description: where the line is expected to start inside the generated clip (LTX measured about 0.75 s, VL-06)

reaction_cover.description: the reaction or insert shot that covers this line's pause

crop.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] as shares of the frame; null = the whole frame

continue_frame.description: continuation: how the start frame is taken from the clip before (our self-hosted LTX has no extend, so the next clip is generated from this frame)

state_changed_since_anchor.description: did anything in the frame change since the anchor photo (upscale direction II.3, finish/superres.decide): false lets a crop or a still come from the 2K anchor photo instead of the softer clip frame; null = unknown, treated as changed

next_use.description: what this shot's hand-over frame feeds (upscale direction II.3): the next LTX clip at the same framing, a punch-in, a still (2.5D, freeze, Short, thumbnail) or nothing

crop.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] as shares of the frame; null = the whole frame

reuse_of.description: this shot reuses another shot's clip or picture with a new framing

intentional_silence.description: SP-04 (sound_plan.design_of): this shot is silent on purpose; a sentence with the reason, never true. Only the room tone plays.

sound_design.description: SP-04: the shot's authored sound design (sound_plan.design_of reads it); today only the silence sentence

silence.description: the reason this shot is silent (same as intentional_silence; one of the two)

audio_balance_target.description: Flexible episode-level guardrail (~65-85% narrator, ~15-35% character dialogue). The screenplay is the master commander; dialogue appears only where dramatic tension requires it.

visual_mix_target.description: Flexible target guideline (~60% video, ~30% illustration, ~10% map); not a rigid quota.

voice_description.description: FA-02 (voice-caster): how this character sounds, in plain words for the LTX prompt (age, timbre, accent, pace), e.g. 'a hoarse older man, low and slow'; never a real person's name

voice_card.description: Q5 (the creator 2026-11-13, D-138; voice-caster): the four facets of the ONE fixed voice text, each found word for word in voice_description; the composer puts that text verbatim into every LTX prompt of the character

ambience_bed.description: FA-09 (story-architect): the place's own bed, authored once; sound_plan takes the bed from here, never from the prose

room.description: the room the bed and its reverb sit in

segment_mode.description: Whether this segment is narration-led exposition/chronology, a played dramatic scene, or a visual-action sequence.

why_a_scene.description: For played_scene segments: what this scene shows (decision, conflict, discovery, reversal) that narration alone cannot deliver.

mood.description: SP-05 / FA-09: the segment's authored mood (sound_plan.segment_mood); a mood read from words is only a candidate

music.description: SP-05: score this segment (true) or let the place's bed carry it (false)

av_contract.description: AV-02 (D-135): a locked script whose every action and motion item carries event_id and audio

schema.description: /2 (2026-10-19): every line carries its visual beats (VB rules, PV-39 FAIL); /3 (2026-10-19, the scene rewrite): dialogue lives in scenes (segments[].scene, lines[].to, SC rules PV-48), cues are opt-in and event-bound (VB-08/VB-10/VB-11); /1 is the legacy contract; /4 (2026-11-01, the MrBeast-style rhythm, BP-169..172): an optional episode.rhythm_profile, a segment rhythm_zone and a shot dramatic_change (BP-170); /1-/3 scripts resolve to the calm_docudrama profile

short_form.description: a pilot of about three minutes: SC-05 asks BP-70's min_exchange_lines_short (2) and only REVIEWs (creator 2026-11-07)

gemini_exception.description: the creator's recorded exception letting Gemini paint this episode's own pictures (D-44 style); without it a Gemini paint plan FAILs PP-05

distinct.description: what makes this episode its own (PV-38): compared with docs/episodes.json

rulebook.description: episode_rules.json next to the script (D-51); new-style scripts set it and PV-39..PV-42 apply

scenario.description: PV-45, OR-15: the short scenario the creator approved before this script was written (file next to the script, sha256 binds the approval)

script_approval.description: PV-53, OR-17: the creator approved this finished script (approval #1) before any paid step; sha256 binds the approval to every word said (scripting/script_approval.py)

promises_sha256.description: the three packaging promises the creator approved with the script (drama.packaging_promises); a changed promise is a PV-53 FAIL

rhythm_profile.description: BP-169: the rhythm profile this script is written for; absent = the profile of its schema version (edit/rhythm_profile.py)

style.description: how the narrator sounds, in descriptive words only (never a real person's name: no imitation, no cloning)

world.description: the world spec read by world.resolver.resolve (host, visitors, light owner, day_arc)

style_refs.description: picture ids that carry the channel look (Gemini frames)

environment.description: the creator's pick from ONE variant collage (OR-16, PV-47): the chosen tile becomes the reference; or, when the creator waived the collage, first_picture: the hero's first scene picture becomes the reference once the creator OKs it on the contact sheet

first_picture.description: the creator waived the collage (2026-10-20): drawn first in its scene in the episode's approved style

continuity.description: D-69: auto stages every segment that has scene.place and no staging block

cast.description: named heroes: how the narration names them, how a picture draws them, what they own

voice.description: the hero's own voice for spoken dialogue lines (D-45): a description of the sound, never a real person to imitate (PV-10, PV-32)

traits.description: VC rules: the character's audible traits (age, gender, temperament, energy, origin), from which audio/casting.py builds the voice search; for a real person only documented traits, never an imitation

ethnicity.description: VC-05: the hero's ethnic or national background, from which the accent is read when origin names none (a Japanese businessman speaks English with a Japanese accent)

living.description: a real person who is alive (D-62, PV-55: a living person's lines are never voiced)

documented.description: sourced facts about a real person's speech (era, origin, temperament); claim ids or URLs

expressions.description: VB-06: expression -> a cut-out face/pose PNG of this hero (the face inset swaps it on every change)

face_sheet.description: VB-09: one sheet of close-up expressions on chroma green, painted once from the hero's reference picture and reused in every scene and episode (production/faces.py)

speech.description: PV-46, DW-11: how the hero talks - from their generally known manner (public, with sources) or, for an invented hero, their personality; our own words, never a quote or an actor's delivery

max_contractions.description: DW-11 register: contractions per word this hero may use at most (0 = none); over it is a REVIEW

mlu_range.description: DW-11 register: [min, max] mean words per turn; outside it is a REVIEW

reference.description: the creator's pick from ONE variant collage (OR-16, PV-47): the chosen tile becomes the reference; or, when the creator waived the collage, first_picture: the hero's first scene picture becomes the reference once the creator OKs it on the contact sheet

first_picture.description: the creator waived the collage (2026-10-20): drawn first in its scene in the episode's approved style

forbidden_props.description: objects that must never be shown (a magnifier when the story's lens is reading glasses)

library.description: pictures that already exist (made in an earlier version): id -> picture

sound_dirs.description: folders (relative to the script) with sounds by name

picture_dirs.description: folders (relative to the script) with the pictures' files

text.description: exactly what is said, no tags

tags.description: ElevenLabs delivery tags placed before the line

emphasis.description: the one word that carries the surprise (spoken in capitals)

voiced.description: D-62 (PV-55): false = the line is never read by a voice; it is shown as speech bubbles, held for reading (BP-27). A real living person's lines are always false

new_read.description: D-63: a narrator line written after the read was recorded (it replaces a run of silent lines); the audio step records only these and reuses the rest

pause_after.description: a held pause after the line in seconds, written as [pause] / ... for the voice and enforced by pause_pad

speaker.description: cast id of the hero who speaks this line in their own voice (D-45, PV-32); absent = the narrator

to.description: SC-04 (/3): who this line is said to - a cast id of scene.present, 'self' or 'room'; a hero never talks to the narrator

intent.description: what the line DOES in the exchange (DW-05/DW-12); a reveal expects another character's reaction

kind.description: Narrative classification for the editorial gate; fact, analysis and speculation require claim references.

visual_beats.description: VB rules: the visual beats of this line (stage 2b, beat-writer), in the order they land

card.description: a line read over a story card (intro or chapter recap, design/cards.py)

at.description: the words of this segment where the picture appears; the cut goes in the pause before them

reported.description: the key phrase of a turn the narrator tells in his own words (creator 2026-10-21: a reported exchange keeps its bubbles)

reuse.description: SR-08 plan: 'unique' or 'reuse' (the picture appeared before; a different crop, zoom or bubble)

accents.description: MO rules: drawn motion accents on top of the camera move, rendered by production/accents.py

at.description: the words the accent lands on (default: the shot's start)

text.description: pop_text / slam_text: the words shown (at most 4)

purpose.description: why this picture is on screen now (PV-42 REVIEW when missing)

cut.description: why the cut or transition into this shot suits the beat (the type stays in transition/UR-14)

purpose.description: the event's narrative or emotional job (PV-41)

beds.description: ambience changes inside the segment, each from its phrase until the next change (crossfaded); a story sound starts on its event's words

purpose.description: the event's narrative or emotional job (PV-41)

period.description: the time-jump chapter this segment belongs to (day1, week1, month1, year1, year10, year100, compare)

scene.description: SC rules (docs/STORY_ENGINE.md, PV-48): the staged scene this segment's dialogue plays in; required on a production_script/3 segment with any speaker line

place.description: where this plays, concrete (the back room of the club, night)

time.description: when, relative to the story (that night, an hour later)

present.description: cast ids physically in the scene; only they may speak or be spoken to (SC-04)

why_now.description: what just changed that forces this conversation NOW

pov.description: the cast id whose want drives the scene

want.description: the pov hero's short-term, concrete want in THIS scene

obstacle_want.description: the opposing want of another present character (SC-03: must differ from want)

value.description: the value at stake (control, trust, safety)

open_charge.description: the value's charge when the scene opens

close_charge.description: the charge when it closes; SC-02: must differ from open_charge or the scene is a nonevent

turn.description: the beat where the scene turns, in one sentence

exit.description: how the scene ends: a failure that sets a new goal, a success that costs, or an interruption

surface_topic.description: what the characters talk ABOUT on the surface (SC-10)

real_subject.description: what the scene is REALLY about; no line may state it verbatim (SC-10)

mode.description: the scene's conflict mode (DW-09: learner is one mode among several, varied across the episode)

drama.description: what this segment does in the story (ST rules): its function, how it follows the one before (but / therefore), the stakes, the value that turns, the loops it opens and closes

turn.description: ST-02: every segment after the first follows by BUT or THEREFORE, never AND THEN

stakes.description: what is lost if it goes wrong, in plain words

shift.description: the value that turns in this segment, as 'from -> to' (safe -> hunted)

claim_share.description: ST-09: what kind of statement carries this segment

job.description: what this beat does for the viewer (EPISODE_STANDARDS 5.4, PV-39)

feel.description: what the viewer should understand or feel at the end of the beat

rules.description: rulebook rules this beat must respect

staging.description: D-69 (CS rules, docs/PRODUCTION_SCRIPT.md): the scene state every picture of this continuous scene keeps; production/staging.py

scene_id.description: the same id on consecutive segments = one continuous scene

continues.description: continues the previous segment's scene (same room, same moment)

layout.description: where things are in the room (the bench along the left wall, the doors behind it)

fixed.description: details every shot keeps (tall oak doors, a cold fluorescent strip)

roster.description: cast ids in the room; left out = scene.present, else everyone the scene's pictures draw

positions.description: cast id -> where they sit or stand, written left to right as the master frame sees them

master.description: the picture id of the master frame; left out = the first wide picture with the whole roster

asset_ids.description: D-70 stage F (Scene Package): asset library ids this segment reuses (assets/library.json)

new_assets.description: Scene Package: assets this segment must make (picture ids or library ids to register)

hash.description: production/segment_hash edit hash the review was given on; a changed segment needs a new review

review.description: Scene Package: the creator's review of this segment

rhythm_zone.description: BP-169: the zone this segment starts in (optional; the zone at its start time otherwise)

voiced.description: D-62 (PV-55): false = the line is never read by a voice; it is shown as speech bubbles, held for reading (BP-27). A real living person's lines are always false

speaker.description: cast id of the hero who speaks this line in their own voice (D-45, PV-32); absent = the narrator

to.description: kept when a Short reuses a scene line (SC-04); not checked on a Short's own lines

visual_beats.description: VB rules on a Short (SS-09): the visual beats of this line, same contract as a segment line's

style.description: SS-01: the Short's style; a set of 10 uses at least 6 styles

counter.description: ED-15 (PV-54): the on-screen time counter; from the first shot of each listed segment the corner shows its label until the next entry

drama.description: the story layer (ST rules, docs/STORY_ENGINE.md): premise, the dramatic question, the hero arcs, the open loops and the set-ups the segments open and pay off

premise.description: the alternate reality in one sentence: what is changed, for whom

question.description: the dramatic question the whole video answers (ST-01)

promise.description: what the viewer gets by the end; the title and thumbnail make this promise

template.description: the beat template of docs/STORY_ENGINE.md: A three-act, B Save-the-Cat, C mystery ladder, D historical docudrama (ST-17..ST-19)

packaging_promises.description: the three title-and-thumbnail promises of the chosen variant (BP-135, stage 1b), copied by the architect; the first is paid in the first seconds (ST-01) and the creator's script approval locks them (PV-53 promises_sha256)

profile_id.description: the structure profile of the chosen variant (BP-141); ST-24 and the spine read it

needs.description: the human needs the episode serves (ST-08); at least three

arcs.description: cast id -> want, need, flaw, change (ST-04)

cards.description: story cards drawn by design/cards.py (the creator 2026-10-21): the dark title card that opens the episode and the chapter recap boards; each is a picture (engine existing) a shot plays

bible.description: D-70 stage F / WB-04: the World Bible version the script was written under (world.bible.cite())

av_audio.description: AV-04 (episode/events.py, D-135): the one audio decision of this visible event; sfx and ui_cue name a class of episode/sound_plan.EVENT_CLASSES; silent_by_design and review_required give their reason

sync.description: onset: starts on the event's first frame; span: lasts the event (continuous action); end: lands on its arrival
